## 1. The one command

```powershell
cd D:\Project\deepseek_harness\public_work\zimage-bfp16-npu
imaggers\repro\t22_run.ps1 -Size 512 -Steps 8 -Tag mytag
imaggers\repro\t22_run.ps1 -Size 128 -Steps 1 -Tag small
```

That is the whole interface: a size, a step count, a tag.  Do not export
anything, do not copy an env block out of a report.  The script sets every
variable itself (section 3), deletes every other device switch it
inherited (section 4), refuses to start if the device is not provably idle
or the size is not renderable (section 5), runs the job, and then proves
which path actually ran (section 6).

### 1.1 the three arguments, including the tag rules

* **-Size** -- a shape (`512` or `512x384`).  512 takes the chunked
  path, 128 the native one.  Any integer per side is accepted, the internal
  grid is 16 px, so a size off that grid is PADDED and cropped back by the
  product (T22-PAD-CROP-REPORT.md).  P05 refuses -- before the device is
  touched -- whatever webui/capability.py cannot render in this env.
* **-Steps** -- the reference table keys on shape+steps, so a new step
  count RECORDS a reference on its first run instead of comparing (Q12).
* **-Tag** -- the name of THIS run, and it is a FILENAME KEY, so its rules
  are enforced, not suggested:
    * charset `A-Za-z0-9._-`.  Every other character (a space, a
      slash, a colon) becomes `-`, leading/trailing `-` are stripped and
      the result is cut to 40 characters; empty becomes `t<HHMMSS>`.
      When anything changed, the engine prints `[tag] <given> -> <used>`.
    * it names `imaggers/repro/last/<tag>.preflight.json`, `...job.json`,
      `...postflight.json`, `...device.json`, `...server.out.log`,
      `...server.err.log`, and ONE row of `last/index.json`.
    * **reusing a tag overwrites that history**: save_run() keeps one row
      per tag, so a second run under the same tag REPLACES the first one's
      row.  Use a fresh tag per run; when you do not, the engine prints
      `[tag] WARNING ... will be OVERWRITTEN` and names the files.
    * it is also the JOB PREFIX, `repro_<tag>`, so the artefact is
      `repro_<tag>_<job-id>_p0_s<seed>.png`: a tag you can read in a
      file name is a tag you can find the record of.
    * a device-collision retry appends `-r2` (RETRY_ON_COLLISION), and the
      retried run writes its records under THAT tag.

What "it worked" means is defined once -- section 6 -- and printed by every
run: **N evaluated, 0 FAIL**, never "N/N PASS".  A native shape has four
checks that are structurally N/A, so no native run can ever print "18/18".

**Read section 12 before comparing any two numbers from this box**, and
section 13 before quoting `startup_s`: the first is the
power-state rule (measured: startup_s x1.50, an 8-step loop x1.075), the
second is the per-second decomposition of a number nobody could
previously attribute.  Only AC numbers are comparable to the references.

Maintenance verbs, not needed to run a job:

```powershell
imaggers\repro\t22_run.ps1 -Action doc                 # regenerate this file
imaggers\repro\t22_run.ps1 -Action preflight -Size 512 -Steps 8 -Tag t
imaggers\repro\t22_run.ps1 -Action postflight -Tag t
imaggers\repro\t22_run.ps1 -Action status
imaggers\repro\t22_run.ps1 -Action cache                 # resolve the B-repack cache
imaggers\repro\t22_run.ps1 -Action cache -Build           # build it once, timed
imaggers\repro\t22_run.ps1 -Size 512 -Steps 8 -Tag off -Extra T22_BREPACK_CACHE=0
```

## 2. What this is for

A 512^2 8-step run of this recipe measured loop 94.15 s and 93.94 s in two
independent arms and produced the SAME latents sha256 (2abf91331200d069...).
The same shape on the product-default env measured 229.26 s and a DIFFERENT
sha (12eb356024a95971...).  Both are real runs of real code; only one of
them is the reference.  Every precondition that separates them is silent
when wrong, which is what this file removes.

Two conventions to read those shas correctly, because both were inferred the
hard way:

* A latents sha256 is **64 hex characters**.  The 16-character prefixes in
  this prose (`2abf91331200d069`, `12eb356024a95971`) are abbreviations for
  reading; section 7 prints the full value and Q12 compares all 64.  The
  16-hex `env_id` is a DIFFERENT thing -- the recipe's label, not the bytes.
* The acceptance sentence is `N evaluated, 0 FAIL` (section 6), not
  `N/N PASS`: a SKIP is a structural N/A and never a pass.

That id is the sha256 of the sorted 34 `name=value` lines, cut to 16
hex.  It is the ONLY label that covers the whole recipe: P06 computes it

It is NOT the same thing as `job.json:env_flags`.  That records

moves the 512^2 latents.  A check that read only `env_flags` could
therefore never be the whole-recipe proof this runbook needs (section 6.2):
the whole-recipe proof is the env_id, and the byte proof is Q12.

## 5. Preflight -- it refuses to start unless all of these pass

| id | check | why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| P01 | repo tree + both interpreters | a wrong path fails before anything else can be trusted |
| P02 | device actually idle (processes, not the lock) | the device is shared and has no real mutex; two users = 0xc01e0009 |
| P03 | lock file: absent, or stale-with-dead-owner | a crashed run leaves a lock that blocks the next launcher |
| P04 | memory mode will be 'fast' (proved, not read) | low mode is 2x slower AND a different latent baseline |
| P05 | size is renderable per webui/capability.py | a refused size dies at submit with an unhelpful HTTP 400 |
| P06 | the job env is EXACTLY the recipe | an inherited switch is a different device path |
| P07 | thread counts the product will apply | loop and VAE threads are coupled unless both are pinned |
| P08 | every device image the path registers exists | a missing image looks like a code bug 60 s into the run |
| P09 | wpack artifact + B-repack cache (both present and reusable) | an ABSENT wpack costs the job ~30 s (a present one is map+verify, ~1-2 s); an UNREUSABLE B-repack cache costs it 27 s -- the largest single row of startup_s -- and looks exactly like a cache that works, so it is a refusal and Q18 is the in-log proof |
| P10 | free disk for images + PNGs | a rebuild of the 5.31 GB B-repack cache and the PNGs need room |
| P11 | last run of this recipe+shape proved its path | a number from an unproven run is not a reference -- and the run it reads must be THIS recipe+shape (env_id, size, steps), not whatever happened to be recorded last by any agent |
| P12 | power state is AC (numbers comparable to references) | on battery the same recipe measured startup_s x1.50 and total_s x1.23 of AC (loop only x1.075); a WARN, never a refusal -- the number is real, just not comparable |

P02 is the real device gate: **a device.lock that is absent means nothing**
(run_job_py.py:31-33 unlinks it at startup, and a launcher that bypasses
that script never writes one).  Measured on 2026-11-03 at 16:05: a
webui\bridge.py dispatch with 9.72 GB resident, actively on the NPU, with
**no lock file present**.  P02 waits up to 1800 s for the device to go quiet,
then FAILS instead of racing it.

P04 does not read a counter and hope: it **allocates 6 GiB and touches every
page**, because that is what the --cache-all pass needs.  If the product's
own auto rule would pick low (commit < 9.0 GB), the job is submitted with
memory_mode=fast explicitly and the preflight says so in its PASS detail.

P04 has a cost the check does not report about itself: the 6 GiB it touches is anonymous memory, so it evicts
exactly the page cache the job is about to read (the 1.99 GB wpack
artifact, the 3.71 GB payload shards).  Measure it as a WITHIN-PAIR
comparison, where the power state cancels:

```powershell
imaggers\repro\t22_run.ps1 -Size 128 -Steps 1 -Tag p04on
imaggers\repro\t22_run.ps1 -Size 128 -Steps 1 -Tag p04off -Skip P04
```

P06 has one WARN: an `--extra` arm that names a RECIPE variable.  The
value really changed, so the expected env is the recipe WITH the arm, the
arm is printed and stored, and the record's `env_id` is the arm's --
not the recipe's.  That is how the two startup arms of section 13 are
measured without a second recipe file, and why neither is mistaken for a
reference run.

P06 is the ONLY place the ENTIRE recipe is compared BEFORE the run: it
checks all 34 variables in the environment the child is about
to inherit, and its `env_id` is the label of that comparison.  The
postflight does not trust the label on its own -- Q11 level 2 re-derives
the id from the env P06 stored (section 6.2).  That label -- not
`job.json:env_flags`, which can see only 12 of the 34 -- is what makes a run's
configuration provable, and it is why section 6.2 has two levels.

P11 reads the last run recorded for THIS recipe and shape -- same env_id,
same size, same steps -- and says whether it proved its path.  It is NOT
"the last run of anything": another agent's 384^2 arm is not your
predecessor.  When there is no such run it SKIPs (not a failure: Q12
records the reference on first use) and quotes the last run of anything
only as context.

P12 records the power state and WARNS on battery; it never refuses, because
a battery number is a real number -- it is just not comparable.  Section 12
is the rule; section 13 is what `startup_s` is made of.

## 6. Postflight -- it proves WHICH PATH RAN, not that the job exited 0

### 6.1 what "it passed" means

The registry below has **18 checks**.  A run is ACCEPTED iff
**FAIL == 0**, over every one of them.  That is the whole rule, and every
run prints it right after its table:

```text
ACCEPTED: 18 evaluated, 0 FAIL -- the path proof holds and the job's number is usable
```

* **SKIP is not a pass.**  It marks a check that is STRUCTURALLY N/A on
  this run's path (the `applies to` column below), and it is printed with
  the ids it skipped so nobody has to guess which one, or why.
* **WARN is not a refusal.**  It is a number to read and act on (the
  total-wall decomposition, the power state, an --extra arm).
* **"18/18" is not a thing.**  A 128^2 native run comes back 13 PASS +
  1 WARN + 4 SKIP + 0 FAIL: 18 evaluated, 0 FAIL, and that is a pass.
  "N/N PASS" was never available on the native path, and a reader who
  expected it had to decide for themselves whether the run had passed.
  The engine prints this definition (ACCEPTANCE_RULE in the generator)
  after the table, so a run's console carries its own acceptance rule.

| id | check | applies to | evidence it reads |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q01 | job finished 'done' | both paths | job.json status + the first exception line of job.log |
| Q02 | the shape took the path the plan named | both paths | '[t18] CHUNKED SEQ=<M>' vs '[t18] SEQ=<M>' |
| Q03 | chunk_path description names the big-M projector | chunked path only | '[t18] chunk_path installed: <what> (proj/ffn/o = ...)' |
| Q04 | fastglue 8/8 hooks installed | chunked path only (fastglue is installed by chunked.install()) | '[fastglue] installed N/8 hooks (threads=T)' |
| Q05 | fastglue hooks WERE CALLED (per-layer lines) | chunked path only (same install) | '[fastglue] layers.N proj_qkv ...' x layers x steps |
| Q06 | FFN: devkill rows + ffnchain calls | chunked path only (its [ffnprof] half is a fastglue hook) | '[devkill] rows=M pack=...' and '[ffnprof] seq=M ...' x layers x steps |
| Q07 | memory mode actually used is 'fast' | both paths | '[webui] memory mode: fast (...)' + '[t13] cache-all: ...' in any of its four shapes (N GB free before allocation / B payloads mapped from / payload already resident / preload is on a worker thread) |
| Q08 | VAE loader actually used (lean vs diffusers) | vae=1 jobs only | '[vae] resident decoder loaded ... [lean]' |
| Q09 | VAE decode thread count actually used | vae=1 jobs only | '[vae] decode threads: torch intra-op N (ZIMAGE_VAE_THREADS=...)' |
| Q10 | loop thread count the server recorded | both paths | job.json env_flags.ZIMAGE_CHUNK_THREADS |
| Q11 | the run's env == the recipe (flags + whole-recipe env_id) | both paths | TWO levels: job.json env_flags (the LAUNCH_FLAGS the product records -- a subset of the recipe) AND the env the preflight recorded, whose env_id is re-derived over EVERY recipe variable |
| Q12 | latents reproduce the reference sha256 | both paths | job.json latents_sha256 vs the reference table |
| Q13 | wall inside the reference windows (loop, and the total decomposed) | both paths, in two parts (each needs its own reference number) | job.json timing.loop_s vs the reference loop_s, AND startup_s + loop_s (the diffusion core) vs the reference total_s, with the excess split between loop seconds and startup seconds |
| Q14 | no device/host fault strings in the log | both paths | the fault strings themselves |
| Q15 | product timing closure gate | both paths | job.json timing.closure.pass |
| Q16 | output image exists at the requested size | both paths | job.json images[0] path/width/height/sha256 |
| Q17 | image set registered at startup | both paths | '[t3d] registered N images: <names>' |
| Q18 | the B repack was MAPPED, not re-derived | both paths (the --cache-all site maps on native too) | an arming line -- '[bigm] B payloads mapped from ...' or '[t13] cache-all: B payloads mapped from ...' (whichever consumer fires first) -- plus '[brepack] HIT ... in N s' and '[devkill] B repack at startup: ~0.0 s', and NO 'repacked once', 'cache unavailable', 'cache MISS' or 'B order: mapped' |

The four that matter most:

* **Q04 vs Q05** -- installed 8/8 is not called.  Q05 counts the per-layer
  [fastglue] layers.N proj_qkv lines and requires exactly layers x steps.
  A run that installs and then never calls the hook FAILS here.  Both are
  CHUNKED ONLY: webui/chunked.py:988-1012 installs the hooks inside the
  ZIMAGE_BIGM + T22_DEVKILL arm of chunked.install(), which a native shape
  never reaches.
* **Q06** -- the same for the FFN chain: [devkill] rows=M lines AND
  [ffnprof] seq=M lines, each layers x steps.  That is why T22_FFN_PROF=1
  is in the recipe: without it the ffnchain hook has no call evidence at
  all, only installation evidence.  Q06 is SKIPped on the native path for a
  PRECISE reason, not a vague one: the [devkill] lines DO run there (30
  "[devkill] rows=96" lines per step, measured on 20261103-194246-47673d),
  but [ffnprof] is emitted by the fastglue install, which is chunked-only --
  so the check could only ever FAIL on native, and a structural N/A is the
  honest answer.
* **Q11** -- section 6.2: the env is proved at two levels, and only the
  second one is the whole recipe.
* **Q13** -- section 6.3: the wall is gated, and the total is DECOMPOSED
  into the loop and the startup it is made of.

### 6.2 Q11 -- the env check has TWO levels, and only one is the whole recipe

Q11 reads `job.json:env_flags` first.  That is `LAUNCH_FLAGS` (webui/config.py:
131-136): 16 names, 12 of them recipe variables.  It is a SUBSET, and no
amount of reading it can prove the other 22 -- `T22_REF_SMNB` among
them, the one variable section 3 says moves the 512^2 latents.  A PASS
line that says "the whole recipe" while comparing a subset is exactly the
trap a cold reader fell into, so both levels are printed now:

(the two lines below are one printed line each, wrapped for width)

```text
LEVEL 1 job.json env_flags: all 16 keys equal, but that tuple is
  LAUNCH_FLAGS -- 12 of the 34 recipe variables -- so 22 are
  INVISIBLE to it (T22_BIGM_DEBUG, T22_DEVKILL_G, T22_DEVKILL_PREWARM, T22_DEVKILL_BREPACK, ...)
LEVEL 2 env_id: the 34 values P06 recorded re-derive to cfc618522d695a67,
  which IS this file's recipe id
```

* Level 2 is RE-DERIVED from the env stored in `last/<tag>.preflight.json`,
  not read from a string, so a stale label cannot fake it (a mismatch
  between the stored label and the re-derivation is reported).
* If that record is missing -- a postflight re-run in a later session --
  level 2 is a WARN and the line says the whole-recipe claim was NOT made:
  only level 1's subset was compared.  Run the preflight and the
  postflight from the same invocation (the `run` action does) to keep it.
* A reference whose `env_id` differs from today's recipe is **not** a
  failure: the 512^2 x8 reference arms were measured under the pre-cache
  recipe id (section 12), and a byte-neutral variable joining the recipe
  cannot move bytes.  Q11 compares the ENV of this run; Q12 compares the
  BYTES -- and Q12 is the only one of the two that can catch a wrong
  `T22_REF_SMNB`.

### 6.3 Q13 -- the wall has a gate, and the total is decomposed

Q13 has two parts and one verdict.

* **loop_s** -- a WARN window of +-25% around the reference loop.  It
  is not a byte gate (two identical-sha 512^2 arms differed 0.2%), but a
  swing that large usually means a different path.
* **the total wall** -- which had NO gate at all, so a reader had to decide
  alone whether a 186.2 s total against a 124.9/135.7 s reference (i.e.
  +37..48%) was a failure.  Comparing `total_s` directly is wrong twice
  over: the reference arms ran `vae=False` while this engine submits
  `vae=True` (+~10 s at 512^2), and `startup_s` is the 15-30 s row that
  moves with the power state and with the B-repack arm (sections 12, 13).
  So the gate is on the **diffusion core = startup_s + loop_s** -- for a
  vae-off arm that IS its total minus the child's import/TE, ~1 s --
  against the reference total, with a +-20% window
  (CORE_TOL in the generator).  For a `vae=yes` reference row the band
  is ~10 s looser (its total carries the decode the core does not), which
  is the safe direction: it can miss a slow run by that much, it cannot
  fail a good one by it.

When the core is outside that window Q13 DECIDES instead of reporting:

* **the excess is in startup_s -> WARN.**  The number is real and it is
  not the loop; sections 12/13 and Q18 name what moves startup.  The
  186.2 s case is exactly this: loop +6.2% (inside its window) and startup
  68 s instead of ~40 s -> WARN, not a failure, and no re-run needed.
* **the excess is in the loop -> FAIL.**  The diffusion work itself is
  outside its window, so the number is not comparable to the reference
  (Q12 still decides whether the bytes are right).

The FAIL branch cannot be reached by the power state alone: the measured
cross-state drift of a multi-step `loop_s` is x1.075 (section 12)
against a +-25% window, while what the power state does move is `startup_s`
(x1.50) -- which is the WARN branch.  A FAIL here therefore means the
diffusion work, not the box.

The split is printed, so "the total is +40%, but the loop is +6% and
startup is 68 s" is in the record instead of in somebody's head:

```text
core startup +68.39 + loop 99.87 = 168.26 s vs reference total 124.9 /
  135.7 s (+24.0%, window +-20%); job total_s 186.19 s; excess +32.56 s =
  5.82 s loop + 26.74 s startup, so 82% of it is startup
```

| 128x128:1 | native | 96 | yes | ba89b71cfd1dfaa089c371e1aab563257885cdcaf3e149b8e71f0826ef1f7673 | 9.11 | - | 20261103-165433-6ab50a |
| 128x128:8 | native | 96 | no | 3c0065d704632b62433272f406cc29cdff521f3b92ab09247d74afc4bb78e0f4 | 21.61 | 50.8 | 20261102-212947-1c18e0 |
| 1920x1080:1 | chunked | 8192 | yes | 7ba858a69f68e0bd0453d219a58b4e8fec18c4d589c97cc2b7b1317363a96696 | 173.72 | 247.5 | 20261104-121901-563011 |
| 384x384:1 | chunked | 608 | yes | 559804dc4a2906a574d196cfb8beddd4df200644a325922de4417e0d1c728343 | 9.41 | 29.3 | 20261103-202344-c36f87 |
| 384x384:8 | chunked | 608 | yes | e4975c41e5d68b795c168ed405f132a0dd9b594903c06a77f36c561010bee414 | 75.47 | 98.3 | 20261103-202743-5f8787 |
| 512x512:1 | chunked | 1056 | yes | 395177106cea950bb640ea94af218871dd680d0d63aa215b111784c31de62e54 | 12.61 | 75.1 | 20261103-181259-014e72 |
| 512x512:8 | chunked | 1056 | no | 2abf91331200d0697d5582e16619db69cad9e387ca95137d18c234be38e84d6e | 94.05 | 124.9 / 135.7 | 20261102-211411-109ea0, 20261102-213051-7c90ae |

A key absent from this table is RECORDED on the first run of that
shape+steps and compared from then on (imaggers/repro/reference.json).

**The sha256 column is the whole value, all 64 hex characters, and that is
what Q12 compares.**  The 16-character prefixes used in this document's
prose (`2abf91331200d069`, `ba89b71cfd1dfaa0`) are abbreviations for
reading only.  Do not confuse the two 16-hex strings in this file: the
latents sha256 is 64 hex, the `env_id` is 16 hex, and neither is a
prefix of the other.

**The `total` column is not one quantity either**, which is why its rows
are not directly comparable:

* `vae=no` -- a reference arm measured with the VAE stage OFF: its
  total is startup + import/TE + loop.
* `vae=yes` -- a run of this engine (which submits vae=True): its
  total includes the decode, +~10 s at 512^2.

That is exactly why Q13 gates the DIFFUSION CORE (startup_s + loop_s) against
the reference total instead of total_s against total_s (section 6.3), and it
is why the loop wall is only a WARN: two runs with identical latents differed
0.2% in loop and 8.7% in total, because the 14.5-19.4 s B repack lands inside
total and outside loop.

## 8. Reading a result

| file | what is in it |
|---|---|
| imaggers/repro/last/<tag>.preflight.json | every check, its PASS/FAIL and the reason, plus the ENV this run had and its env_id (Q11 level 2 re-derives that id from this file) |
| imaggers/repro/last/<tag>.device.json | what the device looked like when the job ended: the lock line, any other device process, the port (section 9.1) |
| imaggers/repro/last/<tag>.job.json | the driver-side copy of the job record |
| imaggers/repro/last/<tag>.postflight.json | the path proof, per item |
| imaggers/repro/last/<tag>.server.err.log | the server's own stderr |
| webui/jobs/<id>/job.log | the authoritative product log the postflight reads |
| webui/jobs/<id>/job.json | memory_mode, env_flags, timing.closure, latents_sha256 |
| imaggers/repro/reference.json | references recorded by earlier runs |

The exit code is 0 only if no check FAILed.  That is section 6.1 in one
sentence: **N evaluated, 0 FAIL**; WARN and SKIP are printed and never fail
a run.  A run whose checks all pass still prints a `[device] ...` line at
the end -- the device state AFTER the job is deliberately not part of the
proof (section 9.1), because another agent's job may legitimately own the
NPU by then.

## 9. When it fails

| symptom | meaning | what to do |
|---|---|---|
| P02 keeps printing a pid | somebody else's job -- or a killed server's orphaned bridge -- owns the device | wait.  Do NOT delete the lock.  If the pid is gone but P02 still sees it, re-run.  Killing another session's bridge is how a run dies mid-dispatch |
| P02 sees a bridge.py and no lock file | a launcher bypassed run_job_py, so no lock was ever written | nothing to clean: P02 is the gate, the lock is only a hint |
| P03 says stale lock, owner alive | a live process owns it | wait for it; the check refuses to steal |
| P04 reserve probe FAILED | the fast path's ~6 GB of commit is not there | close memory and re-run.  Starting anyway means --no-cache-all (2x slower, different latent baseline) or a mid-run MemoryError fallback |
| P05 refused | webui/capability.py refuses this size in THIS env (the fastglue projection BO covers 1632 rows, or the whole-shape BO covers M rows) | read the refusal: it names the exact bytes/rows.  A big-M shape needs T22_ADAPT_M at startup, which is a DIFFERENT recipe and not this one |
| P07 FAIL | ZIMAGE_CHUNK_THREADS and ZIMAGE_VAE_THREADS are unbalanced | they are pinned here; a failure means the product's own derivation moved |
| Q01 fails with 0xc01e0009 ('Failed to create context virtual') | another process took the NPU between this run's preflight and its device stage.  The F-14.1 lock cannot stop it: that launcher never checks the lock (see P02's note) | the tool retries by itself under a new tag suffix (RETRY_ON_COLLISION).  If it still fails, wait for the other session; deleting the lock does nothing |
| Q04 installed 0/8 or 4/8 | T22_FASTGLUE (no underscore) is missing, or a gate failed | the loop is ~40% slower and the run still works -- this is the most expensive silent fallback in the repo |
| Q06 RuntimeError devkill needs n32 B payload | T22_BIGM_DEVHANDOFF is not 1, so prod_loop_bigm hands out {n128,n64} | set it (RECIPE does).  It costs an hour if you believe the lock/payload story instead |
| P09 B-repack cache NOT REUSABLE | the file the recipe's identity resolves to is absent, the wrong size, or built for a different identity (the key covers the 60 source shas, the five permutation functions and the geometry) | build it once, on purpose, and time it: -Action cache with -Extra BUILD.  Do NOT start the job 'to let it build itself': that is the 27 s permutation paid inside startup_s, which is what the recipe removes |
| Q18 found 'repacked once' / 'cache unavailable' / 'cache MISS' | the cache was present (or not) and the run paid the permutation anyway: 27.02 s of a 45.64 s AC startup, with byte-identical latents, i.e. no symptom anywhere else | read the token Q18 names.  'repacked once' means the identity MISSED (a stale file); 'unavailable' means the consumer raised; 'cache MISS' means no file matched.  None of them is a successful run of this recipe.  ONE failure is EXPECTED and is not a fault: an --extra arm with T22_BREPACK_CACHE=0 is the negative control of section 13's pair, and Q18 failing on it is the proof that Q18 can see a miss at all |
| Q07 memory_mode low | the job ran --no-cache-all | its number is not comparable to a fast-mode reference; delete it |
| Q11 FAIL, LEVEL 1 (the env_flags line) | the env the PRODUCT recorded is not this file's RECIPE | the engine scrubs inheritance, so something else launched the server -- check how the run was started |
| Q11 FAIL, LEVEL 2 (the env_id line) | the env P06 recorded does not match the recipe this file defines NOW | either the recipe changed after the run (the number belongs to the old recipe: re-run) or the preflight record is another run's.  LEVEL 2 re-derives the id from the stored values, so a stale label is reported separately from a real difference |
| Q12 sha mismatch while Q11 passes | same env, different bytes | run it twice: same sha twice means the reference is wrong; two different shas mean the path is not deterministic |
| Q14 state 8 | the ERT watchdog fired: two back-to-back launches of the SAME xclbin with no barrier between them (F-01) | keep T20_FFN_BARRIER=1; a completion right after a relaunch may be FALSE (a second kernel handle reports 2-4 ms for a 132.7 MB stream) |
| Q13 says the total wall is outside its band | the diffusion core (startup_s + loop_s) moved, and Q13 prints how much of the excess is startup and how much is loop | read the split -- do not re-derive the decision by hand: excess in startup_s is a startup number (sections 12/13: power state, B-repack arm) and NOT a path failure; excess in the loop is a FAIL and the number is then not comparable to the reference |
| Q11 WARN 'LEVEL 2 env_id: NOT PROVABLE from this record' | there is no preflight record for this tag, so the env_id over the WHOLE recipe could not be re-derived -- only the subset the product records | run the preflight and the postflight in one invocation (the run action does).  Never read level 1 (env_flags) as the whole recipe: see 6.2 |
| P11 SKIP 'no run of THIS recipe+shape has been recorded yet' | nothing has been recorded for this shape+steps under this env_id | not a failure: Q12 RECORDS the reference on this run's first use and compares against it from the next run on |
| a run ends with 'device.lock: held by another pid N -- NOT touched' | another agent's run owns the device; this engine refuses to delete a live owner's lock, which is exactly what P03 is for | do nothing to the lock and do not start a second job.  The postflight reads files only, so finish it now; the next run's P02 waits for that pid (section 9.1) |
| '[run] WARNING device still busy Ns after the server stopped' | an orphaned bridge, or another session's process, was still on the NPU when this run ended | not a failure of your job: P02 waits for it on the next run, and killing another session's bridge is how a run dies mid-dispatch (section 9.1) |

### 9.1 after the run: the device states, and which one means trouble

A finished job leaves the device in one of the states below.  The engine
prints it when the server stops (`[run] post-run device state: ...`) and
again at the end of the postflight (`[device] when this job ended /`
`[device] now`), and stores it in `last/<tag>.device.json`.
**None of these is part of the path proof.**  The postflight reads FILES
only and never touches the NPU, so it is valid even while somebody else's
job owns the device -- including the "held by another pid" case, which is
the one a reader is most likely to mistake for a failure.

| what it says | what it means | what to do |
|---|---|---|
| `device.lock: released (pid N, owner provably dead)` | the clean case: this run took the F-14.1 lock, its server is dead, and the engine removed it | nothing.  The device is not held by this run any more |
| `device.lock: absent` | no lock existed when the server stopped: this launcher never took one, or another script unlinked it (run_job_py.py:31-33) | nothing.  P02 -- processes, not the lock -- is the device gate |
| `device.lock: held by another pid N -- NOT touched` | SOMEBODY ELSE owns the device: another agent's run took the lock while this job was finishing.  The file is THEIRS and this engine refuses to delete another owner's lock (that is what P03 is for) | do NOT delete the lock and do NOT start a second job.  Your job has already finished, and the postflight reads FILES only, so run it now, even with the NPU busy; the next run's P02 waits for the other pid |
| `device.lock: owner pid N still alive -- NOT touched` | the lock is THIS run's, but its server process has not exited yet (the 20 s terminate window elapsed) | wait ~20 s and run -Action status; a pid that never dies is a hung server, not a lock problem |
| `[run] WARNING device still busy Ns after the server stopped: [...]` | an orphaned bridge or another agent's process was still on the NPU when this run ended | not a failure of your job.  The next run's P02 waits for it; do not kill another session's bridge |

## 10. Platform laws a fresh agent must not re-learn

* **F-01** -- state-8: a second back-to-back launch of the same xclbin never completes; the ERT watchdog (~7.0 s) reports state 8.  Any other xclbin's launch clears it -- that is what T20_FFN_BARRIER=1 does. A second kernel handle reports a FALSE completion  (docs/KNOWN-PLATFORM-FACTS.md F-01/F-04, webui/evidence/T20-STATE8.md)
* **F-08** -- at most 7 declared data arguments per kernel; 8/9/10 all ABORT in under 2 ms (add an argument and the kernel dies instantly)  (docs/KNOWN-PLATFORM-FACTS.md F-08, HANDOFF.md:168-170)
* **F-14** -- the device is a shared resource; a second user gets 0xc01e0009.  One process, one xclbin, one context.  device.lock is a protocol, not a mutex  (docs/KNOWN-PLATFORM-FACTS.md F-14, this file's P02)
* **F-09** -- teardown crashes are normal and the exit code is not evidence; the judge is the artefact plus the log line  (docs/KNOWN-PLATFORM-FACTS.md F-09)

## 11. What this runbook does NOT prove, and the code fixes that would

Each item below is a silent fallback this harness works AROUND.  Fixing it
in code would make the workaround unnecessary:

1. `webui/chunked.py:100-105` -- torch.set_num_threads(n) has NO log line, so the loop's effective thread pool cannot be proved from a run
   fix: print once after the first _torch(): [t18] loop threads: torch intra-op N (one line, no behaviour change)
2. `imaggers/util/glue/install.py:869` -- install() prints installed N/8 and returns success even when hooks are missing; the caller ignores the returned state
   fix: chunked.install() should record STATE in the job (or print one [t18] fastglue hooks=N/8 line) so a partial install is a number, not a log line somebody has to notice
3. `webui/chunked.py:995-998` -- an exception inside glue install is printed as [fastglue] skipped and the run continues on the slower path
   fix: raise in trial mode, or set a job-level warning the UI shows
4. `imaggers/block/bigm/prod_loop_bigm.py:647-649` -- T22_DEVKILL=1 with T22_BIGM_DEVHANDOFF!=1 returns {n128,n64}, and the mismatch only surfaces 60 s later inside devkill_ffn.py:332
   fix: raise at startup in cached_payloads() when devkill is on and the handoff payload is absent, with the sentence at devkill_ffn.py:332 instead of a traceback from inside the loop
5. `imaggers/bigpipe2/run_job_py.py:31-33` -- the lock is unlinked at startup WITHOUT checking the owner, so a live job's lock disappears and a crashed job's lock is never diagnosed
   fix: refuse when the owner pid is alive: the same 8 lines as this file's P03
6. `imaggers/bigpipe2/launch_webui_bigm.py:63` -- the lock's purpose string is the literal bigm2_512_1024 whatever the run is
   fix: take the tag/shape from argv so the lock names the run it blocks
7. `webui/config.py:148-163 + webui/vae_local.py:81-92` -- ZIMAGE_VAE_THREADS unset silently inherits the LOOP's thread count, which moves 4-7 pixels of 786,432 at 512^2 -- and when both are 0 nothing is logged at all
   fix: always log the effective count, including the torch-default case, and make the inheritance explicit (auto -> N, follows ZIMAGE_CHUNK_THREADS)
8. `webui/shapes.py:580-583 + webui/capability.py:214` -- chunk_gate() returns a refusal sentence for a shape that is renderable on the NATIVE path, and capability.describe() passes it through, so describe(128,128)['refusal'] is non-empty on a working size
   fix: blank refusal when path != refused (one condition)
9. `webui/runner.py:524-527` -- the MemoryError fallback to --no-cache-all is a log line plus a memory_reason; the job still reports done
   fix: add job['degraded']=True and a [webui] DEGRADED banner: a consumer that reads only status cannot tell
10. `imaggers/image/t18_run.py:196 + imaggers/util/glue/install.py:591` -- T22_FAST_GLUE and T22_FASTGLUE are two different switches one character apart, with opposite defaults (0 vs 1) and different effects
   fix: let install() treat T22_FAST_GLUE=1 as consent when T22_FASTGLUE is unset, or rename one of them
11. `webui/config.py:131-135` -- T22_BREPACK_CACHE is not in LAUNCH_FLAGS, so the JOB's own record cannot say which of the two startup arms it was.  The recipe label (env_id) does cover it, and Q18 reads the consumer's own line -- but neither is in job.json, so a consumer of the product record alone still cannot tell
   fix: add it to LAUNCH_FLAGS (recording only, it selects nothing), so the job record itself distinguishes a mapped run from a repacked one
12. `webui/config.py:37,231,267` -- ZIMAGE_FFN_IMAGE / T22_QKV / T22_P10 default ON while every other device path defaults OFF, and env_flags cannot tell 'default' from 'explicit'
   fix: record the resolved value plus whether it came from the env or the default, so a record cannot be misread as a deliberate choice

Known blind spots of the postflight itself:

* The loop's EFFECTIVE torch thread count has no product log line.  Q10
  reads the value the server recorded plus a runtime probe of the same
  code path, which is the strongest evidence available today (fix 1).
* Of the 8 fastglue hooks, 2 (attn, ffnchain) have per-call log lines and 6
  do not.  Q04 proves all 8 installed; Q05 and Q06 prove 2 of them ran.  A
  call count for the other 6 needs fix 2.
* The PNG sha is recorded, and gated only once a reference exists for that
  exact shape+steps; it is byte-stable only at a fixed thread count.
* Which startup arm a run was in is provable from the log (Q18) and
  from this run's `env_id` (Q11 level 2, which covers
  `T22_BREPACK_CACHE`), but NOT from `job.json:env_flags`: that is
  not in `LAUNCH_FLAGS`, so the job record alone cannot distinguish a
  mapped run from a repacked one (fix 11).
* `job.json` itself carries no env dump, so the whole-recipe proof
  (Q11 level 2) rests on the preflight record this tool wrote.  If that
  record is gone, the claim downgrades to a WARN instead of being faked.

## 12. Power state -- what is comparable to what

This box is a laptop and its wall time moves with the power state.  The
project already recorded that, twice:

* P33-E2E-REPORT.md section 7: the machine was on battery ~08:20-10:10 on
  2026-11-03 and on AC after that; the SAME configuration measured
  89.98-94.45 s on AC and 96.5-135.4 s on battery, and the battery-era
  numbers were DISCARDED rather than compared.
* imaggers/bigpipe2/cyc/CYC-REPORT.md: hardware cycle counts do not move
  with the power state; every WALL time does.

Those two anchors are directional only: neither was a same-recipe pair.
On 2026-11-03 the pair WAS measured -- same tree, same recipe (env_id
0880daf30c579271, i.e. the recipe BEFORE `T22_BREPACK_CACHE=1` joined it),
same shape, ONE latents sha per pair, once on battery and once on AC,
minutes apart:

| metric | shape | battery s | AC s | battery / AC | battery - AC |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `loop_s` | 512^2 x8 | 99.87 | 92.87 | 1.075 | +7.00 |
| `startup_s` | 512^2 x8 | 68.39 | 45.64 | 1.498 | +22.75 |
| `total_s` | 512^2 x8 | 186.19 | 150.94 | 1.234 | +35.25 |
| `loop_s` | 128^2 x1 | 8.73 | 5.73 | 1.524 | +3.00 |
| `startup_s` | 128^2 x1 | 49.41 | 34.93 | 1.415 | +14.48 |
| `total_s` | 128^2 x1 | 68.47 | 48.38 | 1.415 | +20.09 |

Jobs: battery 20261103-171112-09bfbe + 20261103-171717-97cdd7, AC 20261103-183357-58b472 + 20261103-183756-2f06c3.

**The recipe id moved.**  0880daf30c579271 was the recipe with the
B-repack cache SCRUBBED; adding `T22_BREPACK_CACHE=1` to the
recipe (2026-11-03 ~19:20) made the id **cfc618522d695a67**.  Every number in
this section belongs to the OLD id -- it was measured with the 27 s
permutation PAID -- so it is a calibration constant for the power state,
NOT a baseline for a run of today's recipe.  Section 13's pair is the
comparable measurement, taken inside one power state.

That is the coefficient this project never had, and its SHAPE is the
finding: `startup_s` and `total_s` move x1.42-1.50 with
the power state while `loop_s` at 512^2 x8 moves x1.075.  A 68 s
startup in a battery record is therefore NOT a 68 s startup -- and it is not
a code regression either, because the latents sha and the loop did not move.
At 128^2 x1 the LOOP moved x1.52, because a 1-step loop carries torch's
first call (section 13).  A 1-step job is a startup measurement, not a
compute measurement.

So the power state is PROBED and RECORDED, never assumed, and it is the
first thing to check before calling a difference a regression.

| what | how | what it gives you |
|---|---|---|
| AC / battery | `ctypes.windll.kernel32.GetSystemPowerStatus` | `ACLineStatus`: 1 = AC, 0 = BATTERY, 255 = unknown |
| the plan | `powercfg /getactivescheme` | `381b4222-f694-41f0-9685-ff5bb260df2e` = Balanced (shipped plan) |
| magnitude | sha256 over 64 MiB, ~0.2 s | MiB/s travels with every record
  as `power.sha256_mib_s`, so a run carries its own speed index |

Probes that DO NOT work in this session -- all access-denied, written down
so that nobody reads "no battery object" as "a desktop":
`Get-CimInstance Win32_Battery`, `Get-CimInstance Win32_ComputerSystem`,
`Get-CimInstance -Namespace root/wmi -ClassName BatteryStatus`,
`Get-CimInstance -Namespace root/cimv2/power -ClassName Win32_PowerPlan`,
`Get-CimInstance Win32_Processor`, `powercfg /batteryreport`.

The ones that DO work: `powercfg /getactivescheme` (the plan),
`powercfg /query SCHEME_CURRENT SUB_PROCESSOR PROCTHROTTLEMAX`,
`Get-Counter` (works, e.g. `% Processor Performance`), and the ctypes
kernel32 probe above -- which is the one this file records.

THE RULE:

* **Quote, compare and gate AC numbers only; a battery number is real but is readable only against another battery number taken minutes apart -- never against an AC reference.**
* Two numbers may be compared only if both records carry the SAME `power.state`,
  the same recipe `env_id`, and neither is an `--extra` arm.
* Numbers that MAY cross states: `loop_s` of a multi-step job, and
  then only as a magnitude (x1.075 measured at 512^2 x8) -- never as a gate.
* Numbers that may NOT cross states: `startup_s` (x1.50), `total_s` (x1.23),
  every startup phase (x1.3-3.0), `vae_load_s`, `bridge_import_s`, and the
  `loop_s` of a 1-step job (x1.52, because it carries torch's first call).
* On battery: compare WITHIN a back-to-back pair, minutes apart.  Do NOT
  compare a battery number to an AC reference, and do NOT call the
  difference a code regression.
* If the state was not recorded, the honest answer is "unknown, power state
  differs" -- not a percentage.
* `startup_s` is a WALL, so it moves with the power state.  Its
  COMPOSITION (section 13) is power-independent; its magnitude is not:
  the same 45.64 s of AC work is 68.39 s on battery.

## 13. What `startup_s` is made of, and how to re-derive it

`startup_s` is ONE span: the child bridge's first `@@WEBUI@@` event
-> the `startup_done` event (webui/runner.py:1400-1416).  It is big
because it is the payload-residency pass, and none of it is the loop:

| phase | what it costs | where it is printed |
|---|---|---|
| `wpack_verify` | map + sha256 the 1.99 GB prewarm artifact (ZIMAGE_WPACK_VERIFY=1) | [t22] prewarm: ... sha256 verified in N s (webui/bridge.py:591-650) |
| `devkill_prewarm` | pack the 120 G=15 projection W images (chunked path only) | [devkill] prewarm: 120 G=15 ... in N s |
| `brepack_hit` | map the pre-permuted payload from the repack cache (T22_BREPACK_CACHE=1, in this recipe): 60 stat() + a header parse + a 5.31 GB sha256/multiset verify -- this row REPLACES brepack_pass and payload_load | [brepack] HIT ... in N s |
| `warm_wpack` | pack the 30 layers' projection images from the mapped artifact | [t3d] warm: 30 layers' projection images packed in N s |
| `payload_load` | read + permute the 3.71 GB BG/B3 payload (--cache-all) | [t13] full-memory cache: 30 layers, 3.71 GB in N s |
| `brepack_pass` | the 5.31 GB in-place B-order permutation.  With the cache mapping it is only the join+arm (measured 0.0x s); it is the 27.02 s row when the cache is off or misses, which Q18 gates | [devkill] B repack at startup: N s |
| `refiner_weights` | map the refiner blocks the first step needs (noise_refiner.0/1, 2 x 0.67 GB); context_refiner.0/1 land AFTER startup_done and are not in this bucket | [t3d] refiner weights loaded noise_refiner.N  N s |
| `bridge_jit` | the unprinted remainder: the child's torch/numba import, the fastglue byte gates, the 19 image registrations and the chunked projector install -- split per second in the AC ledger below | no line -- startup_s minus the rows above |

A job's own log already carries each of those seconds, so the decomposition
is re-derivable from artefacts alone -- no instrumentation and no guess:

```powershell
py312 imaggers\startup\compose.py <job-id> [<job-id> ...]
```

MEASURED 2026-11-03, same tree, same recipe, seconds:

| phase | 512^2 x8 06:30 (state NOT recorded) | 512^2 x8 17:11 (battery) | 512^2 x8 18:33 (AC) | 128^2 x1 17:17 (battery) | 128^2 x1 18:37 (AC) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| wpack_verify | 1.15 | 2.10 | 1.61 | 1.85 | 1.43 |
| devkill_prewarm | 2.41 | 6.10 | 3.94 | 0.00 | 0.00 |
| brepack_hit | 3.02 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 |
| warm_wpack | 2.50 | 3.50 | 1.70 | 4.00 | 1.40 |
| payload_load | 0.00 | 9.70 | 3.20 | 9.10 | 4.30 |
| brepack_pass | 0.00 | 31.73 | 27.02 | 31.58 | 26.20 |
| refiner_weights | 1.40 | 2.50 | 1.20 | 1.90 | 1.00 |
| bridge_jit | 2.65 | 12.76 | 6.97 | 0.98 | 0.60 |
| **`startup_s` total** | **13.13** | **68.39** | **45.64** | **49.41** | **34.93** |

Three things follow, and together they answer "is 68 s a regression":

1. The COMPOSITION changed.  The 06:30 arm had `T22_BREPACK_CACHE=1`,
   inherited from its shell, so it MAPPED a pre-permuted payload and paid
   3.02 s; the 17:xx and 18:xx arms ran the recipe AS IT WAS THEN, which
   SCRUBBED that switch, so they paid the real 5.31 GB permutation
   (brepack_pass) AND the 3.71 GB payload read (payload_load) that a
   mapped cache makes free.  That is ~38-41 s of the difference and it is
   work the Nov-2 reference did not do either.  It is not a slow machine
   and it is not a re-defined bucket: the bucket boundaries are unchanged
   since 06:30 (both arms report the same `startup_child_s` == `startup_s` split), only the WORK inside it changed.
   AS OF 2026-11-03 ~19:20 the recipe SETS the switch (section 3), so this
   table is the LAST measurement of the un-mapped arm -- kept because it
   is the baseline the pair below is measured against.
2. The MAGNITUDE changed too.  Every phase that BOTH arms pay is slower on
   battery, and the two AC arms (18:33/18:37, same recipe, byte-identical
   latents) size it: wpack verify 1.61 -> 2.10, devkill prewarm 3.94 ->
   6.10, warm wpack 1.70 -> 3.50, payload load 3.20 -> 9.70, refiner 1.20
   -> 2.50, i.e. 1.3-3.0x per phase.  That is the power-state drift of
   section 12, not code.
3. THE POWER SHARE IS NOW A MEASURED NUMBER, not a range: `startup_s` 45.64
   on AC -> 68.39 on battery (x1.50), `loop_s` 92.87 -> 99.87
   (x1.075), `total_s` 150.94 -> 186.19 (x1.23).  So of the 68.39 s,
   **22.75 s was the power state and 45.64 s was work the recipe really
   did** (27.02 s of it the B repack, which the recipe now MAPS instead
   -- the pair below).  Neither is a regression: a regression moves the
   latents and the loop, and neither moved.

### the B repack removed -- WITHIN-WINDOW pairs


#### 512^2 x8 -- battery, 2026-11-03 19:23:43 - 19:38:2x, back to back

Same tree, same recipe, same shape, same power state; ONE value differs (T22_BREPACK_CACHE).  The second OFF arm is the drift check: it ran after the ON arm, so the pair shows how much the box moved while the measurement was being taken -- for free, because the run was needed anyway.  P02 recorded 'no device process' before each arm, and the P12 speed index is quoted per arm.

| arm | `T22_BREPACK_CACHE` | battery | P12 speed | job | latents sha16 | `startup_s` | `loop_s` | `total_s` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| OFF #1 | 0 | 68% | 1127 MiB/s | 20261103-192343-658254 | 2abf91331200d069 | 47.24 | 95.09 | 156.29 |
| ON | 1 | 67% | 1321 MiB/s | 20261103-192702-8edbf1 | 2abf91331200d069 | 17.15 | 97.15 | 131.64 |
| OFF #2 (drift) | 0 | 64% | 989 MiB/s | 20261103-193520-085610 | 2abf91331200d069 | 63.97 | 99.53 | 182.28 |

| phase | OFF #1 | ON | OFF #2 (drift) | ON - mean(OFF) |
|---|---|---|---|
| wpack_verify | 2.02 | 1.88 | 1.88 | -0.07 |
| devkill_prewarm | 5.41 | 3.40 | 5.81 | -2.21 |
| brepack_hit | 0.00 | 3.45 | 0.00 | +3.45 |
| warm_wpack | 1.40 | 2.90 | 3.70 | +0.35 |

Every arm carries the same latents sha16 (Q12 is the gate), so the
table is a cost difference and nothing else.  `loop_s` is
printed because it must not move either: the repack was weight
preprocessing inside startup, never a step.

The 2 OFF arms differ by **16.73 s** of startup_s
-- that is this box's run-to-run spread inside one window (the P12
speed index moves with it: 1127, 1321, 989 MiB/s).  The saving
is therefore quoted against BOTH OFF arms, not against one.

#### 128^2 x1 -- battery, 2026-11-03 19:40:52 - 19:42:46, back to back

The native path (M=96) pays exactly the same startup rows, so the same removal applies: a 1-step job is a STARTUP measurement, not a compute measurement (section 12), which is why the total nearly halves while the loop does not move.

| arm | `T22_BREPACK_CACHE` | battery | P12 speed | job | latents sha16 | `startup_s` | `loop_s` | `total_s` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Every arm carries the same latents sha16 (Q12 is the gate), so the
table is a cost difference and nothing else.  `loop_s` is
printed because it must not move either: the repack was weight
preprocessing inside startup, never a step.

A NEGATIVE `bridge_jit` is overlap, not a missing bucket: the
cache's map+verify (brepack_hit) runs on a worker thread while the
warm pack runs on the main one, so two rows cover the same seconds.
The bucket is still defined as startup_s minus the rows above; it is
the rows that are not disjoint.

### every second of `startup_s` on AC

job 20261103-183357-58b472, 512^2 x8, AC, `startup_s` = 45.64 s.
Row 1 is an anchor delta; rows 2-8 are the product's own log lines; rows
9-11 are the segments no product line prints, measured in the same py310
interpreter by `imaggers/startup/startup_probe.py`; the last row
closes the table.

| bucket | what it is | seconds | where the number comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| shape geometry | patch grid / M / resume-latent geometry | 0.03 | anchor delta first_event -> shape_geometry |
| wpack artifact read | map + sha256 the 1.85 GiB wpack | 1.61 | [t22] prewarm: ... sha256 verified in N s |
| devkill prewarm | pack the 120 G=15 projection W images | 3.94 | [devkill] prewarm: 120 G=15 ... in N s |
| warm wpack | pack 30 layers' projection images | 1.70 | [t3d] warm: ... in N s |
| payload load | read + permute the 3.71 GB BG/B3 payload | 3.20 | [t13] full-memory cache: ... in N s |
| B repack | the 5.31 GB in-place B-order permutation | 27.02 | [devkill] B repack at startup: N s |
| refiner cache read | map noise_refiner.0/1 (2 x 0.67 GB) | 1.20 | [t3d] refiner weights loaded noise_refiner.N  N s |
| image registration | 19 images: 16 big-M + att/attip/ffn | 0.20 | [t3d] registered 19 images: sum of the per-image seconds |
| torch import | the chunked install's _torch() (chunked.py:936) | 1.93 | startup_probe.py, median of 3 |
| numba import | first numba import inside the glue install | 0.24 | startup_probe.py, median of 3 |
| fastglue install | the 8 byte gates + hook install (warms the JIT) | 0.64 | startup_probe.py, median of 3 |
| chunk_path install | big-M whole-shape proj (rt17) + its BOs + [t18] parse + t8 + RESUME -- THE ONLY SEGMENT THE PRODUCT DOES NOT PRINT | 3.93 | startup_s minus the rows above |
| **`startup_s` total** | **the whole span** | **45.64** | first_event -> startup_done |

The `chunk_path install` row is the only part no artefact names.
It is chunked-path work, not device time: the native 128^2 x1 arm's whole
residual is 0.60 s and already contains `[t18]` parse, `t8`, the device
context and 21 image registrations.  On battery this row is 12.76 s
(x1.83) -- the most power-sensitive row in the table, which is the shape
of a memory/CPU-bound install, not a device one.

### the seconds of the same job that are NOT inside `startup_s`

Quoted because they are the buckets people expect to find here (TE init,
the VAE loader, the child's spawn) and they are real -- they are simply
outside the span `webui/runner.py:1396-1424` books.

| segment | seconds | where it is booked |
|---|---|---|
| device child spawn + interpreter + driver import | 0.55 | bridge_import_s: launch -> the child's first @@WEBUI@@ event |
| TE init (text enc cache hit) | 0.01 | timing.textenc_s; the cache is on disk, so this is a read, not an encode |
| wpack prewarm wait | 0.68 | timing.prewarm_pack_s; the packer runs while this job text encodes |
| loop_s (8 steps) | 92.87 | startup_done -> last step; step 0's first layer carries torch's first-call warmup (host 5.54 s for that layer against ~0.3 s steady state) |
| VAE loader | 3.94 | timing.vae_load_s: the lean decoder, after the loop |
| VAE decode + save | 6.22 | timing.vae_decode_s + vae_save_s |

Step 0's first layer is where the loop's own warmup lands: `[tim] img 1/1 first
layer: ... host 5.54 s` on AC (9.80 s on battery) against ~0.3 s of
steady-state per-layer host work in the `[fastglue]` and `[devkill]` lines --
torch's first call, not a diffusion cost.  That is why
a 1-step job's `loop_s` is NOT a compute number (section 12: it moved
x1.52 with the power state, while the 8-step loop moved x1.075).

Re-derive it from the artefacts:

```powershell
py312 imaggers\startup\compose.py <job-id>    # the per-phase rows
py312 imaggers\startup\startup_probe.py 3     # torch/numba/fastglue
```

What `startup_s` does NOT contain: the wpack pack itself.  A present
artifact costs map+verify only; the 33.035 s in its manifest is the BUILD
time from 2026-11-02T15:22:06 and is booked to `prewarm_pack_wall_s`,
which is not a bucket.  An earlier draft of P09 said "33 s of the job's
wall" -- that sentence was the mis-measurement, and P09 now says so.
